docs.title: 🚀 Comandos básicos de Git (primeros pasos)
docs.text: En este curso solo usaremos los comandos esenciales de Git para trabajar con repositorios.

docs.title: 1. Clonar un repositorio
docs.text:
Copia un proyecto de GitHub a tu computadora.

git clone https://github.com/usuario/repositorio.git

docs.title: 2. Verificar cambios
docs.text:
Muestra qué archivos has modificado o agregado.

git status

docs.title: 3. Preparar cambios
docs.text:
Agrega archivos para guardarlos en el próximo commit.

git add archivo.txt
git add .   # agrega todos los archivos modificados

docs.title: 4. Guardar cambios (commit)
docs.text:
Guarda tus cambios con un mensaje descriptivo.

git commit -m "Descripción breve de los cambios"

docs.title: 5. Subir cambios al repositorio (push)
docs.text:
Envía tus commits locales al repositorio en GitHub.

git push origin main

docs.title: 6. Traer cambios del remoto (pull)
docs.text:
Actualiza tu proyecto con los últimos cambios de GitHub.

git pull origin main

docs.title: Flujo típico de trabajo
docs.text:
1. Traer cambios del remoto 

    git pull origin main

  2. Editar tus archivos de proyecto.

  3. Preparar los cambios 

    git add .

  4. Guardar los cambios 

    git commit -m "Mensaje descriptivo"

  5. Enviar los cambios al remoto 

    git push origin main

Consejo

Piensa en este ciclo como un loop infinito: cada vez que quieras contribuir → primero pull, después add + commit, y finalmente push.

docs.title: Session 3 & 4- Register level & GPIO
docs.text:
Goal session 3 (one sentence): Compare the signal and execution time between SDK GPIO timing instructions and registrer-Level.

Prediction: The SDK GPIO has a slower execution so it takes a few extra cycles to run the code. This is why I think the frecuency levels of the register level instructions will be higher

docs.title: Setup
docs.text: • Pin map: GP18 was connected to the LED output and the scope CH1 probe was on GP18

docs.title: What I did
docs.text:
1. I connected my Pico 2 to a breadboard and opened a new project from "Blink" in the VS Code extension.
  2. Ran SDK instructions.
  3. Connected and callibrated the oscilloscope to measure the frequency.
  4. Deleted the SDK and replaced it with register-level instructions.
  5. Use the oscilloscope again with the same settings.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
This image shows the SDK frecuency that was at 792.4 Hz.

This image shows the Register-level frecuency measurement and it was at 1.317 kHz.

docs.title: Session 4
docs.text: Goal session 3 (one sentence): Complete 4 different level exercices that reproduce four classic pattern animations with four LEDs

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
• Pin map: GP10 → PIN_D, GP11 → PIN_C, GP12 → PIN_B, GP13 → PIN_A (4-bit bus, one LED + resistor per pin); pushbutton on the breadboard for reset.

  • Photo of the raspberry Pi Pico setup:

docs.title: What I did
docs.text:
1. Connected the LEDs to GP10-GP13.
  2. Reused the register-level configuration validated in Session 3 (gpio_init per pin + a single sio_hw->gpio_oe_set with a 4-bit mask) instead of the SDK calls.
  3. Wrote the coude for each exercise.

  4. Run each program and recordered it as evidence.

  5. Setuo code we used in the exercises: 

    #define PIN_A 13
#define PIN_B 12
#define PIN_C 11
#define PIN_D 10

const uint32_t MASK =
    (1u << PIN_A) | (1u << PIN_B) | (1u << PIN_C) | (1u << PIN_D);

gpio_init(PIN_A);
gpio_init(PIN_B);
gpio_init(PIN_C);
gpio_init(PIN_D);

sio_hw->gpio_oe_set = MASK;   // OE = Output Enable

docs.title: 4 bit binary counter
docs.text:
Goal is to use the LEDs as a 4-bit-binary number wich counts from 0 to 15 in a cycle. 

int counter = 0;

while (true) {
    sio_hw->gpio_clr = MASK;
    sio_hw->gpio_set = (counter << 10);
    sleep_ms(500);

    counter++;
    if (counter > 15) {
        counter = 0;
        sleep_ms(1000);
    }
}
### Evidence

docs.title: Bouncing light
docs.text:
The goal for this exercise was to move the LED across four positions (0001,0010,0100,1000,0100,0010,0001) and back.

int counter = 0;

while (true) {
    sio_hw->gpio_clr = MASK;
    sio_hw->gpio_set = (1u << (counter + 10));
    sleep_ms(500);

    counter++;
    if (counter > 3) {
        while (counter > 0) {
            counter--,
            sio_hw->gpio_clr = MASK;
            sio_hw->gpio_set = (1u << (counter + 10));
            sleep_ms(500);
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Fill and empty animation
docs.text:
The goal was to turn LEDs on one by one starting from right and going to the left and then turning them off, we did this using a gpio_togl.

int counter = 0;

while (true) {
    sio_hw->gpio_togl = (1u << (counter + 10));
    sleep_ms(500);

    counter++;
    if (counter > 3) {
        counter = 0;
    }
}

docs.title: Fill from the outside inward
docs.text:
The goal was to light the two outer LEDs, then the two inner ones and then turning them off in the inverse sequence

int counter = 0;

while (true) {
    sio_hw->gpio_togl = (1u << (counter + 10));
    sio_hw->gpio_togl = (1u << (13 - counter));
    sleep_ms(500);

    counter++;
    if (counter > 1) {
        counter = 0;
    }
}
